chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear the belittled sins, for they are not forgiven.' I said: 'And what are the belittled sins?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man commits a sin, so he says, 'Good fortune is for me if there had not been for me other than that (sin).''

key_terms.الْمُحَقَّرَاتِ: The belittled or considered minor sins
key_terms.طُوبَى: Good fortune or bliss (often referring to Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What are the 'belittled sins' that are not forgiven according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'al-muḥaqqarāt' as sins a person commits yet considers insignificant, a state of spiritual complacency that prevents their forgiveness. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'tawassu' (expansion) of minor sins in the heart as a barrier to divine mercy, urging believers to treat small transgressions with the gravity of major ones to ensure comprehensive repentance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shahham who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fear the belittled ones from the sins, for these would not be Forgiven’. I said, ‘And what are the belittled ones from the sins?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man commits the sin, so he is saying, ‘Tooba (A tree in the Paradise) would have been for me if there had not happened to be for me other than that (belittled sin)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from abu ‘Usamah Zayd al-Shahham from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following: “Guard against al-Muhaqqarat (sins); they will not be forgiven.’ I then asked the Imam, ‘What is al-Muhaqqarat ?’ The Imam said, ‘A man commits a sin and says, “I will have Tuba (a tree in paradise) if I did not have any other sins.’”
